cells.raw_text: Raised, palpable hemorrhagic skin lesions in the absence of thrombocytopenia
Diffuse abdominal pain or the diagnosis of bowel ischemia
Histologic changes showing granulocytes in the walls of arterioles or venules; IgA deposits in vessel wall
Age <20 years at onset of symptoms
Slightly elevated, potentially related to ongoing inflammatory process.
Negative, ruling out certain types of vasculitis.
From Nelson essentials of pediatrics, 9th ed. p. 362. *The diagnosis of IgA vasculitis is based on the presence of two of four criteria.
